ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure A is a real-scene picture of the hillside slide; Figure B is a geometric schematic diagram, in which A, C, and E form a right triangle, AC is a vertical line, CE is a horizontal line, and AE is the inclined straight-line slide; point D is on AC, and the dashed line DE connects to E. Then reason: From the meaning of the problem, AD＝DE＝10 m. Let AC＝h and CE＝x, then DC＝h－10. In right triangle DCE, DE is the hypotenuse, so x²＋(h－10)²＝10², which simplifies to x²＋h²＝20h. Also in right triangle ACE, AE²＝AC²＋CE²＝h²＋x², therefore AE²＝20AC. The slide is smooth, and the acceleration along the inclined plane is a＝g·AC/AE. Starting from rest and sliding a distance AE along AE, there is AE＝(1/2)at², so t²＝2AE²/(g·AC)＝2×20/10＝4, therefore t＝2 s.
